body.text: The initial fuel is a sodium-bonded metal fuel in a tight, hex-packed pin bundle, with pins separated by a wire wrap.
body.anchor: The pin bundle is arranged in a tight, hex-packed configuration

body.text: The pin has shield slugs at the bottom, a sodium-bonded fuel column in the center, and a gas plenum with a tag gas capsule at the top, inside HT9 alloy steel cladding.
body.anchor: The fuel pin comprises shield slugs at the bottom

body.text: Cladding provides a functional containment barrier and resists plenum gas pressure and fuel swelling.
body.anchor: The fuel pin cladding provides a functional containment barrier

body.text: Tag gas identifies assemblies with failed fuel pins, using an online fuel monitoring system.
body.anchor: Tag gas is used to identify assemblies containing failed fuel pins

body.text: There are nine primary and four secondary control rod assemblies, which work with the CRD.
body.anchor: There are nine primary control rod assemblies and four secondary control rod assemblies

body.text: Absorber pins hold cladded, helium-bonded, boron carbide pellets.
body.anchor: The absorber pins contain cladded, helium-bonded, Boron Carbide absorber pellets

body.text: Scram insertion has enough worth to shut down the reactor and maintain safe shutdown even with the highest worth rod stuck withdrawn.
body.anchor: even if the highest worth rod is stuck in the withdrawn position

body.text: Secondary control assemblies provide a regulating function to manage small reactivity changes.
body.anchor: The secondary control assemblies provide a regulating function

body.text: Reactor power level, start-up, and shut-down are controlled by operator action. No operator action is required for the DL3 scram functions or to initiate natural circulation for emergency decay heat removal.

title: Reactor Core System
subject: RCC
intro: The Reactor Core System is the set of replaceable core assemblies. This lesson covers each assembly type, reactivity control, and what the core must do in an event.

objectives.text: State the purpose of the RCC.
Identify the RCC boundaries and interfaces.
Identify the major components of the RCC.
Describe the RCC controls and indications.
Explain the RCC automatic features and interlocks.
Apply operating procedures for the RCC.
Diagnose abnormal conditions in the RCC.
Explain the safety significance of the RCC.
Address technical specifications and administrative controls for the RCC.
